title: "Sydney's Housing Weakness Was Deepest in Expensive Houses"
description: "Sydney's established-house median fell 4.0% in the June quarter, versus 1.8% for attached dwellings. Higher-value houses had fallen further from peak; the rest was less weak, not rising."
date: "2026-06-11"

categories: [housing, cost-of-living, australia, property-prices, abs]

---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(knitr)

source(file.path("..", "..", "R", "data_sources.R"))

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

raw_dir <- file.path("data-raw", "housing")
source_registry <- read_source_registry("sources.csv")
source_files <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(source_registry)),
  function(index) download_registered_source(source_registry[index, , drop = FALSE], raw_dir)
)
source_manifest <- write_source_manifest(source_files, file.path(raw_dir, "source-manifest.csv"))

source_path <- function(source_id) {
  index <- match(source_id, source_registry$source_id)
  if (is.na(index)) stop("Missing source in sources.csv: ", source_id, call. = FALSE)
  source_files[[index]]$path
}

as_number <- function(x) {
  parse_number(as.character(x), na = c("", "NA", "n/a", "-"))
}

assert_true <- function(condition, message) {
  if (!isTRUE(condition)) stop(message, call. = FALSE)
}

assert_close <- function(actual, expected, tolerance, label) {
  if (length(actual) != 1 || !is.finite(actual) || abs(actual - expected) > tolerance) {
    stop(sprintf("%s did not reconcile. Expected %s; found %s.", label, expected, actual), call. = FALSE)
  }
}

quarter_date_from_excel <- function(x) {
  as.Date(as.numeric(x), origin = "1899-12-30")
}

last_semicolon_field <- function(item) {
  item |>
    str_remove(";\\s*$") |>
    str_extract("[^;]+$") |>
    str_squish()
}

stock_measure <- function(item) {
  case_when(
    str_detect(item, fixed("Value of dwelling stock; Owned by All Sectors")) ~ "Total dwelling stock value",
    str_detect(item, fixed("Mean price of residential dwellings")) ~ "Mean dwelling price",
    str_detect(item, fixed("Number of residential dwellings")) ~ "Number of dwellings",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

parse_abs_stock <- function(path) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Data1", col_names = FALSE)
  metadata <- tibble(
    column = seq_along(raw),
    item = as.character(unlist(raw[1, ])),
    unit = as.character(unlist(raw[2, ])),
    measure = stock_measure(item),
    state = last_semicolon_field(item)
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(measure), !is.na(state), state != "")

  expected_units <- c(
    "Total dwelling stock value" = "$ Millions",
    "Mean dwelling price" = "$'000",
    "Number of dwellings" = "000"
  )
  assert_true(
    nrow(metadata) == 27 && all(metadata$unit == unname(expected_units[metadata$measure])),
    "The ABS stock workbook series or units have changed."
  )

  rows <- raw |> slice(-(1:10))
  names(rows) <- paste0("column_", seq_along(rows))
  series <- rows |>
    mutate(quarter_date = quarter_date_from_excel(column_1)) |>
    select(quarter_date, -column_1, everything()) |>
    pivot_longer(-quarter_date, names_to = "column", names_prefix = "column_", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(column = as.integer(column), value = as_number(value)) |>
    left_join(metadata, by = "column") |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(quarter_date), !is.na(measure)) |>
    mutate(
      value = case_when(
        unit == "$ Millions" ~ value / 1000,
        unit %in% c("$'000", "000") ~ value * 1000,
        TRUE ~ value
      )
    ) |>
    select(quarter_date, state, measure, value)

  assert_true(
    nrow(series) == n_distinct(series$quarter_date) * 27,
    "The parsed stock workbook does not contain 27 complete series."
  )
  series
}

transfer_measure <- function(item) {
  case_when(
    str_starts(item, "Median Price") ~ "Median transfer price",
    str_starts(item, "Number") ~ "Number of transfers",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

transfer_dwelling_type <- function(item) {
  case_when(
    str_detect(item, "Established House") ~ "Established house",
    str_detect(item, "Attached Dwelling") ~ "Attached dwelling",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

parse_abs_transfers <- function(path) {
  raw <- read_excel(path, sheet = "Data1", col_names = FALSE)
  metadata <- tibble(
    column = seq_along(raw),
    item = as.character(unlist(raw[1, ])),
    unit = as.character(unlist(raw[2, ])),
    measure = transfer_measure(item),
    dwelling_type = transfer_dwelling_type(item),
    geography = last_semicolon_field(item)
  ) |>
    filter(!is.na(measure), !is.na(dwelling_type), !is.na(geography))

  assert_true(
    nrow(metadata) == 60 &&
      all(metadata$unit[metadata$measure == "Median transfer price"] == "$'000") &&
      all(metadata$unit[metadata$measure == "Number of transfers"] == "Number"),
    "The ABS transfer workbook series or units have changed."
  )

  rows <- raw |> slice(-(1:10))
  names(rows) <- paste0("column_", seq_along(rows))
  rows |>
    mutate(quarter_date = quarter_date_from_excel(column_1)) |>
    select(quarter_date, -column_1, everything()) |>
    pivot_longer(-quarter_date, names_to = "column", names_prefix = "column_", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(column = as.integer(column), value = as_number(value)) |>
    left_join(metadata, by = "column") |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(quarter_date), !is.na(measure)) |>
    mutate(value = if_else(unit == "$'000", value * 1000, value)) |>
    select(quarter_date, geography, dwelling_type, measure, value)
}

stock <- parse_abs_stock(source_path("abs_total_value_dwellings"))
transfers <- parse_abs_transfers(source_path("abs_dwelling_transfers"))

expected_states <- c(
  "New South Wales", "Victoria", "Queensland", "South Australia",
  "Western Australia", "Tasmania", "Northern Territory",
  "Australian Capital Territory", "Australia"
)
latest_quarter <- as.Date("2026-06-01")
previous_quarter <- as.Date("2026-03-01")
expected_transfer_geographies <- c(
  "Sydney", "Rest of NSW", "Melbourne", "Rest of Vic.",
  "Brisbane", "Rest of Qld.", "Adelaide", "Rest of SA",
  "Perth", "Rest of WA", "Hobart", "Rest of Tas.",
  "Darwin", "Rest of NT", "Canberra"
)

assert_true(max(stock$quarter_date) == latest_quarter, "The stock workbook does not end in June 2026.")
assert_true(max(transfers$quarter_date) == latest_quarter, "The transfer workbook does not end in June 2026.")
assert_true(setequal(unique(stock$state), expected_states), "The stock workbook geographies have changed.")
assert_true(!anyDuplicated(stock[c("quarter_date", "state", "measure")]), "The stock series contains duplicate keys.")
assert_true(!anyDuplicated(transfers[c("quarter_date", "geography", "dwelling_type", "measure")]), "The transfer series contains duplicate keys.")
assert_true(all(is.finite(stock$value) & stock$value >= 0), "The stock series contains invalid values.")
assert_true(all(is.finite(transfers$value) & transfers$value >= 0), "The transfer series contains invalid values.")
assert_true(setequal(unique(transfers$geography), expected_transfer_geographies), "The transfer workbook geographies have changed.")

stock_coverage <- stock |>
  group_by(state, measure) |>
  summarise(
    latest = max(quarter_date),
    complete = identical(sort(quarter_date), seq(min(quarter_date), max(quarter_date), by = "3 months")),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
assert_true(nrow(stock_coverage) == 27 && all(stock_coverage$latest == latest_quarter), "Not every stock series reaches June 2026.")
assert_true(all(stock_coverage$complete), "At least one stock series has a missing quarter.")

transfer_coverage <- transfers |>
  group_by(geography, dwelling_type, measure) |>
  summarise(
    latest = max(quarter_date),
    complete = identical(sort(quarter_date), seq(min(quarter_date), max(quarter_date), by = "3 months")),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
assert_true(nrow(transfer_coverage) == 60 && all(transfer_coverage$latest == latest_quarter), "Not every transfer series reaches June 2026.")
assert_true(all(transfer_coverage$complete), "At least one transfer series has a missing quarter.")

latest_transfer_snapshot <- transfers |> filter(quarter_date == latest_quarter)
assert_true(
  nrow(latest_transfer_snapshot) == 60 &&
    sum(latest_transfer_snapshot$measure == "Median transfer price") == 30 &&
    sum(latest_transfer_snapshot$measure == "Number of transfers") == 30,
  "The latest transfer snapshot must contain 30 medians and 30 counts."
)

headline <- stock |>
  filter(quarter_date == latest_quarter, state == "Australia") |>
  select(measure, value)
assert_close(headline$value[headline$measure == "Total dwelling stock value"], 12688.8568, 0.0001, "National stock value ($ billions)")
assert_close(headline$value[headline$measure == "Number of dwellings"], 11531100, 1, "National dwelling count")
assert_close(headline$value[headline$measure == "Mean dwelling price"], 1100400, 1, "National mean dwelling price")

latest_stock <- stock |>
  filter(quarter_date == latest_quarter) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value)
assert_true(
  abs(sum(filter(latest_stock, state != "Australia")$`Total dwelling stock value`) -
    filter(latest_stock, state == "Australia")$`Total dwelling stock value`) < 0.01,
  "State stock values do not reconcile to Australia."
)

focus_geographies <- c("Sydney", "Rest of NSW", "Melbourne", "Rest of Vic.")
focus_transfer_source <- transfers |>
  filter(
    measure == "Median transfer price",
    geography %in% focus_geographies,
    quarter_date %in% c(previous_quarter, latest_quarter)
  )
assert_true(
  nrow(focus_transfer_source) == 16 &&
    all((focus_transfer_source |> count(geography, dwelling_type))$n == 2),
  "Each focus segment must contain March and June 2026."
)

focus_transfers <- focus_transfer_source |>
  group_by(geography, dwelling_type) |>
  arrange(quarter_date, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    previous_price = first(value),
    latest_price = last(value),
    change = latest_price / previous_price - 1,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    state = if_else(geography %in% c("Sydney", "Rest of NSW"), "New South Wales", "Victoria"),
    area = if_else(str_starts(geography, "Rest"), "Rest of state", "Capital city"),
    segment = paste(area, dwelling_type, sep = " / ")
  )

expected_focus <- tibble(
  geography = c("Sydney", "Sydney", "Rest of NSW", "Rest of NSW", "Melbourne", "Melbourne", "Rest of Vic.", "Rest of Vic."),
  dwelling_type = rep(c("Established house", "Attached dwelling"), 4),
  expected_price = c(1487600, 840000, 810000, 710000, 850000, 590000, 625000, 467800)
)
focus_check <- focus_transfers |>
  left_join(expected_focus, by = c("geography", "dwelling_type"))
assert_true(
  nrow(focus_check) == 8 && all(focus_check$latest_price == focus_check$expected_price),
  "The focus-state June transfer medians did not match the checked ABS values."
)

latest_transfer_counts <- transfers |>
  filter(measure == "Number of transfers", quarter_date == latest_quarter)
assert_true(nrow(latest_transfer_counts) == 30 && all(latest_transfer_counts$value >= 0), "Latest transfer counts are incomplete or invalid.")

# Published Cotality September 2026 chart-pack results, data through August.
# Lower-quartile declines are derived from the published upper-quartile decline and upper-minus-lower gap.
tier_declines <- tribble(
  ~city, ~tier, ~decline,
  "Sydney", "Upper quartile", -0.107,
  "Sydney", "Lower quartile", -0.054,
  "Melbourne", "Upper quartile", -0.105,
  "Melbourne", "Lower quartile", -0.039
)

```

Within New South Wales, June-quarter weakness was sharpest in Sydney established houses. Their median transfer price fell 4.0%, compared with 1.8% for Sydney attached dwellings, 2.4% for rest-of-NSW houses and 0.6% for rest-of-NSW attached dwellings. Cotality's quality-adjusted indexes through August point in the same direction across price tiers: upper-quartile Sydney houses were 10.7% below peak, versus 5.4% for the lower quartile.

That is concentration, not containment. Every broad NSW segment in the ABS data fell, and the public data used here cannot separate inner from outer Sydney. Victoria is a useful comparator, but its pattern was messier. The rest of the market was generally less weak—not broadly stable or rising.

Nor did the concentration last. By September, the downturn had spread across almost every capital-city suburb and into many regional markets. This article therefore separates the question of **where the fall first appeared deepest** from the question of **how broad the later downturn became**.

::: {.callout-note}
## Three measures, three different questions

- **ABS stock values** estimate the value of every residential dwelling. They locate which jurisdictions drove the national fall.
- **ABS transfer medians** describe the middle property sold in a quarter. They split established houses from attached dwellings and capital cities from the rest of each state, but can move when the mix of sales changes.
- **Cotality's hedonic index** adjusts for property characteristics and can compare value tiers. The tier results cited here are published commercial findings; the underlying tier series is not publicly downloadable, so I have not presented them as my own independently reproduced estimates.
:::

## Sydney established houses fell most

The ABS transfer medians provide a first cut by broad geography and dwelling type. Sydney's established-house median fell `r percent(abs(filter(focus_transfers, geography == "Sydney", dwelling_type == "Established house")$change), accuracy = 0.1)` in the June quarter, compared with `r percent(abs(filter(focus_transfers, geography == "Sydney", dwelling_type == "Attached dwelling")$change), accuracy = 0.1)` for attached dwellings. Outside Sydney, both declines were smaller.

Victoria is the useful counterexample. Melbourne houses fell, but Melbourne attached dwellings were close to flat; outside Melbourne, attached dwellings fell more than houses. So the broad NSW pattern—more expensive capital-city houses weakening most—was not a mechanical rule everywhere.

```{r}
#| label: fig-focus-segments
#| fig-cap: "Change in unstratified median transfer price, March to June 2026. 'Attached' generally includes apartments, units, terraces, semis and townhouses, although some NSW terraces and townhouses are classified as established houses. Source: ABS Table 2; June estimates are preliminary."
#| fig-alt: "Two-panel dot plot for New South Wales and Victoria. Sydney established houses fell 4.0 per cent, Sydney attached dwellings 1.8 per cent, rest-of-NSW houses 2.4 per cent and rest-of-NSW attached dwellings 0.6 per cent. Melbourne houses fell 2.9 per cent, Melbourne attached dwellings 0.1 per cent, rest-of-Victoria houses 0.8 per cent and rest-of-Victoria attached dwellings 2.5 per cent."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.2

segment_levels <- c(
  "Rest of state / Attached dwelling",
  "Rest of state / Established house",
  "Capital city / Attached dwelling",
  "Capital city / Established house"
)

focus_transfers |>
  mutate(
    segment = factor(segment, levels = segment_levels),
    emphasis = geography == "Sydney" & dwelling_type == "Established house"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(change, segment)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = change, yend = segment), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = emphasis), size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(change, accuracy = 0.1)), nudge_x = -0.002, hjust = 1, colour = "grey20", fontface = "bold", size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~state, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#6E8794", `TRUE` = "#B8472D")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(-0.065, 0.005), breaks = seq(-0.06, 0, 0.01)) +
  labs(
    title = "Sydney established houses fell most",
    subtitle = "Victoria shown as a comparator; quarterly change in median transfer price",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  )
```

These are not apartment-versus-house price indexes. “Attached dwelling” is broader than apartment, “rest of state” is not the same as regional, and an unstratified median can fall because cheaper homes made up more of that quarter's sales. The latest transfer counts are preliminary and revision-prone, so they should not be read as a collapse in market activity.

## Upper-quartile houses fell further in Sydney and Melbourne

The strongest evidence for the value-tier story in Australia's two largest cities comes from Cotality's quality-adjusted indexes, not the ABS transaction medians. In data through August, upper-quartile houses were 10.7% below their peak in Sydney and 10.5% below in Melbourne. The upper-to-lower decline gaps were 5.3 and 6.6 percentage points respectively.

```{r}
#| label: fig-price-tiers
#| fig-cap: "Published Cotality hedonic-index results through August 2026. Lower-quartile values are derived from the published upper-quartile declines and upper-minus-lower gaps. The underlying tier series is commercial and was not independently reproduced."
#| fig-alt: "Dumbbell chart comparing house-value declines from peak by price tier. Sydney's upper quartile fell 10.7 per cent versus 5.4 per cent for the lower quartile. Melbourne's upper quartile fell 10.5 per cent versus 3.9 per cent for the lower quartile."
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 4.5

tier_wide <- tier_declines |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = tier, values_from = decline)

ggplot(tier_wide, aes(y = city)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = `Upper quartile`, xend = `Lower quartile`, yend = city), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Upper quartile`), colour = "#B8472D", size = 4) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `Lower quartile`), colour = "#6E8794", size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(x = `Upper quartile`, label = percent(`Upper quartile`, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = 1.25, fontface = "bold", colour = "#8F3522") +
  geom_text(aes(x = `Lower quartile`, label = percent(`Lower quartile`, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.25, fontface = "bold", colour = "#536873") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.107, y = 2.38, label = "Upper quartile", colour = "#8F3522", hjust = 0, size = 3.4) +
  annotate("text", x = -0.04, y = 2.38, label = "Lower quartile", colour = "#536873", hjust = 0.5, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(-0.125, -0.02), breaks = seq(-0.12, -0.02, 0.02)) +
  labs(
    title = "Upper-quartile houses had fallen much further by August",
    subtitle = "Cumulative decline in house values from each tier's cyclical peak",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  )
```

This supports the narrower hypothesis that higher-value houses led the downturn in Sydney and Melbourne. It is not a result about the full Australian price distribution, does not mean every expensive property fell, and does not identify the cause. It is also a cited commercial estimate: [Cotality publishes the headline tier findings](https://www.cotality.com/au/insights/articles/high-end-homes-lead-market-downturn-as-affordable-properties-prove-resilient), but not the raw tier series needed to reproduce the index independently.

## Concentrated does not mean contained

Every broad NSW segment in the ABS comparison fell. Across NSW and Victoria, three of the eight segments were within 1% of their March median, but none increased. That makes “the rest was less weak” a better description than “the rest was rising.” It also keeps the limits of unstratified medians in view: changes in the mix of properties sold can move the median even when like-for-like values move differently.

## Inner versus outer Sydney remains unanswered

The national ABS workbook stops at capital city versus rest of state; it cannot tell us whether the weakness sits in Sydney's inner, middle or outer rings. NSW's [property-sales information files](https://www.valuergeneral.nsw.gov.au/design/bulk_psi_content/bulk_psi) could eventually support that analysis, but complete 2026 registrations are not yet available in one annual archive and recent weekly files arrive with lags and revisions.

A defensible inner/outer comparison would need complete transactions mapped to consistently defined rings and, ideally, an adjustment for the changing mix of homes sold. Without that, “rest of NSW” should not be relabelled “outer Sydney” or “regional,” and the geographic split should remain an explicit unanswered question.

## The initially concentrated fall later broadened

The June data describe where the national fall was concentrated, not the latest breadth of the downturn. In September, [Cotality's national index fell 1.1%](https://www.cotality.com/au/insights/articles/australian-housing-values-down-for-sixth-straight-month-in-september). Over the preceding three months, 97% of capital-city suburbs had fallen, and 71% of regional SA3 markets fell in September alone.

Regions were still more resilient—regional values were 5.6% higher than a year earlier while the combined capitals were 1.8% lower—but they were no longer uniformly stable or rising. The clean conclusion is:

> Sydney's weakness was concentrated, not contained. Established-house transfer medians fell more than attached dwellings, and upper-quartile houses had fallen further from peak than lower-quartile houses. But every broad NSW segment fell, the public data cannot resolve inner versus outer Sydney, and by September the weakness had spread much more widely.

## Data and method

The primary calculations use two workbooks from the ABS [Total Value of Dwellings, June Quarter 2026](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/total-value-dwellings/jun-quarter-2026), released 8 September 2026. Table 1 contains whole-of-stock estimates; Table 2 contains unstratified transfer medians and counts. Both latest-quarter sets are preliminary and can be revised. The release-specific [ABS methodology](https://www.abs.gov.au/methodologies/total-value-dwellings-methodology/jun-quarter-2026) defines dwelling types, geographic coverage, estimation and revision rules.

The build verifies each workbook's file size and SHA-256 checksum, expected units and series count, June 2026 coverage, unique keys, national headline values, state-to-national reconciliation and the eight focus-state transfer medians. To deliberately refresh the registered downloads, render with `BLOG_REFRESH_DATA=true`; a changed upstream file fails checksum validation before replacing the cached copy.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-focus-values
#| tbl-cap: "Focus-state median transfer prices, June quarter 2026"

focus_transfers |>
  arrange(state, geography, dwelling_type) |>
  transmute(
    State = state,
    Geography = geography,
    `Dwelling type` = dwelling_type,
    `June median` = dollar(latest_price, accuracy = 1000),
    `Quarterly change` = percent(change, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  kable(align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r"))
```

### Source register

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sources

source_registry |>
  transmute(
    Publisher = publisher,
    Dataset = paste0("[", dataset, "](", landing_url, ")"),
    `Source/revision date` = release_date,
    `Coverage end` = coverage_end,
    `SHA-256 prefix` = substr(sha256, 1, 12)
  ) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l"))
```
